# Vault base

The vault is one autobase with 2 views, the bee (automap) and the audit log (auditcore). One apply sees both views and the base has one set of writers.

```javascript
const { create_vault_base } = require('vault-base')
const base = create_vault_base(store.namespace('vault'), bootstrap) // bootstrap null = new vault
const vault_bee = create_automap({ base })
const vault_audit = create_auditcore({ base })
```

Entries the log appends have `view: 'log'`, everything else (put, del, add / remove writer) goes to the bee. Apply goes through the nodes in order: the bee nodes before a log entry are written first, then the log entry gets `meta.views = { bee: <bee length> }`. When a change and its log entry are in one append (`vault_audit.append(entry, { with: batch.entries })`, like `audit_wrap` in identity-operations does), they are in one apply, so every device gets the same length and `vault_bee.checkout(meta.views.bee)` is the bee right after that change (serapath's REQUEST-1).

Writers are added and removed through the bee (`vault_bee.add_writer`), `vault_audit.add_writer` does nothing on a shared base.

Old vaults (separate `vault-bee` and `vault-audit` autobases) arent read anymore, they need a reset.

1 base vs 2 bases measured in `docs/vault-views-check.js`.

Tests: `bare lib/node_modules/vault-base/vault-base.test.js`
